newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end quiet session higher.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end quiet session higher.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures ended a quiet session firmer on follow-through strength from Monday's late rally, traders said.
"It was not a very exciting day, there wasn't much news to move it," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter.
The trade continued to watch weather developments in Brazil. "South America weather is beautiful, they're in really great shape," Lespinasse said.
Scattered rains fell Tuesday in Brazil's key soybean growing regions but growers in Parana said their crops might suffer if heavy rains continued much longer.
"It's rained too much, said Edson Luiz de Soza, agronomist at the Copagril cooperative in Parana. "If it continues for a few more days then we will have a problem."
On the day, ADM bought four million bushels May and Iowa Grain and Rosenthal Collins each bought three million March.
E.D. and F. Man International, Refco Inc, Rosenthal Collins, SAK Futures and Tenco Inc each sold one million March and Dean Witter sold two million March.
Cargill Inc spread four million March/May and July/May.
Soybeans ended 5-3/4 to 1/4 cents per bushel higher with March up 1/4 at $7.37.
In options trade, Refco Inc sold 500 May $7.75 calls at nine cents and Farmers Commodities Corp bought 275 March $7.75 calls at 1-5/8.
Soybean futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 46,000 contracts, above the 41,677 traded Monday.
Soybean options volume was estimated at 15,000 contracts, above the 14,202 traded Monday.
